# Extra Strings Task - ASCII Art

On this page you will write Python programs which make [ASCII Art](https://www.asciiart.eu). This is a type of [digital art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_art) made with text characters. Here is an [example](https://www.asciiart.eu/art/0c60ec7e5a6ae726) of an ASCII art picture of a bear:

```
    .--.              .--.
   : (\ ". _......_ ." /) :
    '.    `        `    .'
     /'   _        _   `\
    /     0}      {0     \
   |       /      \       |
   |     /'        `\     |
    \   | .  .==.  . |   /
     '._ \.' \__/ './ _.'
jgs  /  ``'._-''-_.'``  \
```

This task is *fun but hard*. You will have to think about how to do it first. Remember that moving away from the computer and using a [pen and paper](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_01_Class_Rules.html#have-a-piece-of-paper-and-a-pen-next-to-you) can help you if you get stuck. You can also work with a partner and try to solve the task with [pair programming](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_01_Class_Rules.html#pair-programming).

This task will help you think about *visual alignment*, a very important concept in programming:

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pxr687/Intro_Comp_Programming/refs/heads/main/images/ASCII_alignment.JPG)
(Image from [here](https://www.lenovo.com/th/en/glossary/alignment/?srsltid=AfmBOoo-YCbAgPRdpe6G4een7oTZ3Oha9yo23580ThHF0LCyDUQKPk4h)).

Visual alignment means values (strings or numbers) are in the right place. The image of the bear above has the right alignment - it looks nice, it looks like a bear.

The image of the bear below this sentence does *NOT* have the right alignment (I broke the bear image to make this mess...): 

```
             .--.              .--.
   : (\ ". _......_ ." /) :
    '.    `        `    .'
     /'   _        _   `\
 0}      {0     \
   |       /      \       |
                    |     /'        `\     |
          \   | .  .==.  . |   /
                          '._ \.' \__/ './ _.'
jgs/  ``'._-''-_.'``  \
```

Visual alignment is **not** just important for ASCII art. It is important when you make websites and apps - anything that a *user sees needs to have good visual alignment*.

*Note*: there are lots of different ways you can do this task. You will need to use what you have learned about strings. There are some tips below.


### Tip 1
Putting strings into variables and then putting the variables together with operators (`+`, `*`) is better than writing the whole image in one string. 

### Tip 2
Using [multi-line strings](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_08_02_More_On_Strings.html#multi-line-strings) can help you complete this task - you do not have to do this, you can solve the task using one line strings if you want to. Here is a quick demo of multi-line strings:
<!-- #endregion -->

```{python}
# A one-line string.
print("This is a string on one line.")
```

```{python}
# A multi-line string.
print( """
This is a string...

...which goes over lots of...

...lines, I can go over...

...as many lines as I want.

To make a multi-line string...

...you use THREE quotation marks...

...to start and end the string.
""")
```

```{python}
# You can also store multi-line strings in variables.
my_multi_string = """
This is a string...

...which goes over lots of...

...lines, I can go over...

...as many lines as I want.

To make a multi-line string...

...you use THREE quotation marks...

...to start and end the string.
"""

# `print()` the multi-line string variable.
print(my_multi_string)
```

### Tip 3
You can also look at the [`.replace()` string method](file:///C:/Users/rushpz/Intro_Comp_Programming/_build/html/1_08_00_Data_Types.html#how-to-avoid-errors-use-type) this will also let you solve this task using less lines of code... Here is a short demo of the `.replace()` string method:

```{python}
# Make the `my_string` variable.
my_string = "Poto1"

# Show the value of `my_string`.
my_string
```

```{python}
# Use the `.replace()` string method. 
# Here I replace the character 'o' with the character 'e'.
my_string.replace('o', 'e')
```

```{python}
# We can use replace lots of times with the same string.
# Here I replace the character 'o' with the character 'e' AND `1` with `r`.
my_string.replace('o', 'e').replace('1', 'r')
```

```{python}
# We can use `.replace()` lots of times AND save the result in a variable.
my_fixed_string = my_string.replace('o', 'e').replace('1', 'r')

# Show the value of `my_fixed_string`.
my_fixed_string
```

**Before** you start writing code, think about how you can solve the task using *the smallest number of lines of code*.
